slides.title: Order requests branch without losing control
slides.takeaway: Long-running work moves to an asynchronous queue while direct writes retain a short synchronous path to Azure Cosmos DB.
slides.subtitle: One decision separates immediate persistence from queued work, while both paths converge on the same order store.

diagram.alt: Rightward flow across three swim lanes: Front Door to AKS, then a decision routes direct writes to Cosmos DB or queued work asynchronously before persistence.

sources.label: Use Azure Front Door to secure AKS workloads

slides.notes: Audience: cloud platform leaders. Purpose: show that the order platform can route long-running work asynchronously without creating a separate persistence model. The diagram is conceptual and does not represent deployed inventory. The Work queue is intentionally service-neutral because no queue technology was specified. Solid connectors show synchronous traffic; dashed blue connectors show asynchronous traffic. The direct and queued paths both persist order state to Azure Cosmos DB.
